summary: Peiros or Peirous (Ancient Greek: Πείρος / Πείροος) is the Thracian war-leader from Aenus, son of Imbrasus, who allies with Priam. In Iliad 4 he slays Diores with a jagged stone and is himself killed by Thoas of Aetolia. The atlas keeps a separate Catalogue node (peirous-thracian); Wikipedia unifies the Homeric spellings on one page.

sections.heading: Thracian captain
paragraphs: Homer places Peiros son of Imbrasus among the Thracians from Aenus. He smites Amarynceus' son Diores on the ankle with a jagged stone, crushing sinew and bone; Thoas of Aetolia then drives a spear through Peiros' breast beside the nipple.
Later notices make him father of Rhygmus, who also fights at Troy. He is not the Achaean river Peiros in the Peloponnese.

sections.heading: Homonyms and spelling
paragraphs: This atlas entry (peiros-thracian) is the battlefield son of Imbrasus. The Catalogue captain Peirous (peirous-thracian) is stored separately; many readers treat them as one Homeric figure under variant spellings.
